small_guidance:
- The kernel uses `allow_tf32=False`, which is a major perf hit on a GEMM this size (M=N=K=8192). Switch to `allow_tf32=True` in `tl.dot` — fp32 inputs from `torch.rand` are within tolerance of the 5e-2 atol/rtol check, and TF32 roughly doubles tensor-core throughput.
- Add larger-tile autotune configs tuned for square 8192³ GEMM on Ada: `BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=256, BLOCK_K=64, num_warps=8, num_stages=3/4` and `BLOCK_M=256, BLOCK_N=128, BLOCK_K=64`. Drop the small `64x256` and `BLOCK_K=32` configs from the search — they lose to K=64 at this size.
- Since M, N, K are all multiples of 128, drop the K-loop masking (use unmasked `tl.load` for the inner loop) and only mask the boundary tiles in M/N to remove per-iter mask compute. Also consider pre-transposing weight to `(K, N)` contiguous so both A and B inner-axis loads are fully coalesced without strided B access.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite around a TF32 (or fp16-accum-in-fp32) tensor-core GEMM. A well-tuned Triton GEMM at 8192³ on a 4090 can hit ~50-70 TFLOPs TF32; the current 4.47 ms implies ~245 TFLOPs of fp32 non-TF32 work, i.e. the kernel is leaving the tensor cores idle. Enabling TF32 alone should close most of the 1.8× gap to the 2.43 ms cuBLAS baseline.
- Consider a persistent-CTA / split-K-free design: launch exactly `num_SMs` programs and have each loop over `(pid_m, pid_n)` tiles in swizzled order. This amortizes scheduling overhead and improves L2 reuse of weight tiles across the M dimension.
- Keep the sigmoid+scale+residual epilogue fused on the accumulator (already done) — the only structural change needed is the GEMM core itself. Do not split the epilogue into a separate kernel.
